reasons: Correct classification: Section 7 contains only a mutual consequential-damages waiver and no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement, so both parties' direct liability is unlimited and the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs) fails on a material term — this is a genuine deviation, not an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and minimal: it leaves the existing mutual consequential-damages waiver (and its indemnification/confidentiality carve-outs) untouched and adds a single new subsection (b) supplying the missing cap, which is the smallest edit that can reach the playbook position where no cap sentence exists to amend.

Substance matches the preferred position: mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts under the Agreement and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, plus an express statement that Section 5 payments are not 'damages' (the analogue of the 'payment obligations are not damages' element).

Adaptation of the cap basis from 'fees paid by Customer' to 'amounts paid or payable between the parties' is justified and disclosed: in a revenue-share structure where Vendor pays Customer, a pure Customer-fees cap would be illusory, and the USD 1m floor preserves a meaningful cap — consistent with the detection guidance on illusory fee bases.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix; it states what changed, why the fixed floor is needed, that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers negotiation room on the floor.

Deterministic checks all pass (cap references 12 months plus a fixed floor; no one-sided or unlimited-Customer language introduced); the added-text volume is inherent to supplying a wholly absent cap rather than an unnecessary rewrite.
